author: Stone Fox Capital
title: Verizon: 5G Pause - Verizon Communications (NYSE:VZ)
text:
The announcement that Samsung ( OTC:SSNLF ) and Verizon Communications ( VZ ) won't launch a 5G phone until next year will likely lead to a pause in Verizon stock. The stock recently hit my target at $60 likely on the back of 5G excitement. The lack of devices to connect to a 5G network should cause the excitement over the new technology to come to a sudden halt.
Image Source: Verizon website
5G Phone Realities While the major domestic wireless providers are fighting over which company will have the first operational 5G mobile network, the market has mostly ignored that the two major phone manufacturers aren't on board with 5G phones yet. Samsung and Verizon released the intent to unveil a prototype phone using the Snapdragon X50 5G NR modem and antenna modules from Qualcomm ( QCOM ).
The news comes as Apple ( AAPL ) appears officially headed towards a 2020 launch of its 5G iPhone. Absent any new killer 5G device, one will find getting too hyped about 5G over the holidays difficult without the Galaxy or iPhone on the market.
According to the summary by FierceWireless , Samsung expects to release the next Galaxy in February, followed by the foldable Galaxy S10. By March, the 5G version should be released, though it won't include the foldable frame.
CNET provides some further detail on the Samsung phones set to be released early next year.
For its part, Verizon has made statements around turning on the 5G network in early 2019. The wireless giant seems to still back this concept with the agreement with Samsung:
Verizon 5G mobility service will go live in early 2019 and expand rapidly. Once available, Samsung 5G smartphone users will immediately benefit from the speed and capacity of Verizon’s 5G Ultra Wideband network, and over time , experience all the new and exciting services, games and features that will be available.
The lack of key devices should slow down any hype surrounding 5G networks. Even Verizon appears to pull back the throttle by saying the network will benefit users over time, not at the start.
About The Stock Verizon recently topped $60, causing JPMorgan to downgrade the stock due to stock gains and a relatively new management team. The stock trading down 3.5% on the news when the market was up big time on a trade truce with China is a sign that Verizon hit a short-term peak.
At the start of the year, Verizon and AT&T ( T ) traded at similar valuations. In the past few months, a huge gap has appeared in the forward P/E multiples of the two largest domestic wireless stocks.
VZ PE Ratio (Forward 1y) data by YCharts
The likelihood here is that investors start rotating into AT&T following its Investor Day last week that confirmed a dividend payout ratio in the high 50% levels. Anything below 60% will attract yield seekers away from Verizon.
VZ Dividend Yield (TTM) data by YCharts
As the stock becomes a source of funds, Verizon will struggle to maintain $60. The dividend yield had already slumped to the lowest levels in the past few years at 4%.
Takeaway The key investor takeaway is that Verizon will likely become a source of funds in order to buy AT&T as that stock trades at the lows. The realization that 5G won't be ready for prime time will hurt the stock as well, after soaring to $60 due to speculation of moving on to the next major network upgrade.
The best time to get back into Verizon is after the new 5G Galaxy comes onto the market and the stock is trading towards the lower $50s. At that point, the company should offer a consistent stream of positive 5G mobility news for the next couple of years, as opposed to the current hype that fueled the recent rally prior to actual launch.
